targets.rawSql: WITH e AS (SELECT at, backend, action, lead(at) OVER (PARTITION BY backend ORDER BY at) AS next_at, lead(action) OVER (PARTITION BY backend ORDER BY at) AS next_action FROM interventions) SELECT at AS time, backend, action AS disabled_by, next_action AS ended_by, round(extract(epoch FROM next_at - at)::numeric, 1) AS seconds_disabled FROM e WHERE action IN ('disabled', 'operator_disabled') AND next_at IS NOT NULL AND $__timeFilter(at) ORDER BY at DESC LIMIT 100

targets.rawSql: SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(finished_at, $__interval), choice AS metric, count(*) AS value FROM jev_assessments WHERE $__timeFilter(finished_at) AND question = 'route' AND status = 'ok' GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Primacy bias: share of 'complex' by option order
panels.description: Jev's route choice split by which option was listed first. Live traffic uses one fixed order today (standard first), so only one bar appears until orders vary. If the two bars differ on the same messages, that is primacy bias.

targets.rawSql: SELECT option_order[1] || '-first' AS "order", round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE choice = 'complex') / count(*), 1) AS pct_complex FROM jev_assessments WHERE $__timeFilter(finished_at) AND question = 'route' AND status = 'ok' AND option_order IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Primacy bias: route choices by option order

targets.rawSql: SELECT option_order[1] || '-first' AS "order", choice, count(*) AS calls FROM jev_assessments WHERE $__timeFilter(finished_at) AND question = 'route' AND status = 'ok' AND option_order IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2

options.content:
The gateway makes **one** Jev call per request, before the model answers. It returns the route and the intent together. There is no second Jev call that scores the model's reply.

What is compared today is the model's intent label against Jev's intent answer: see *Qwen vs Jev intent agreement* above. The standard-first vs complex-first comparison needs the order-swap run (PRs #89, #90).

options.content: Only port 8080 is published. Prometheus, Postgres and the gateway stay on the Compose network. Grafana is reached through the proxy at `/grafana`, as an anonymous **viewer**: no login, no editing. Postgres panels use a read-only database user.
